text:
Maya: Hey team — onboarding two new AWS org accounts and hitting quota blockers. Targets: eu-west-2 (acct 123456789012) and ap-southeast-1 (acct 210987654321). Need increases before next Monday: p5 (all sizes) -> 8 total, p4d -> 4 total, g5 -> 20 total, and ENI quota -> 2000 per region. Can someone open support cases?

Sam: I can open them. Need a short justification and whether these are steady-state or burst. Also: do we want on-demand only or ask for Reserved/Dedicated limits?

Maya: Quick justification: launching production inference pool for customer X (SLA: 99.9%). Expected steady-state 6 concurrent p5 hosts for model serving, peak burst to 12 for scaling tests. p4d for large training/inference jobs (bursty), g5 for mixed smaller workloads. We expect sustained usage after launch. Cost note: we'll amortize with reserved capacity if AWS approves.

Devon: When you open cases, include exact quota codes if possible (service-quotas/Ec2 - Running On-Demand p5 instances, p4d, and g5 categories) and include ENI quota (L-xxxxx). Example case body I usually use:

```
Account: 123456789012
Region: eu-west-2
Requested quota: Running On-Demand p5 instances -> 8 (current 0), p4d -> 4 (current 0), Running On-Demand g5 instances -> 20 (current 2), ENI limit -> 2000 (current 1000)
Justification: Production inference fleet for low-latency model serving for customer X; expected steady-state 6 p5 hosts, burst to 12. Launch date: 2026-03-23. Please expedite if possible; we have a hard SLA and regression tests scheduled.
```

Devon: Also attach our ALB/load test plan and expected concurrent connections per instance. That speeds review.

Linda: Add VPC IDs and subnet ranges for both accounts and cc networking. We saw ENI exhaustion on node-pool-alpha last week — attaching a snippet from kubelet logs: 

```
Mar 12 09:14:22 node-xx kubelet[1234]: E03012 09:14:22.123456    1234 cni.go:234] failed to allocate network for pod "...": Failed to attach ENI: no available addresses in subnet
```

Linda: If we can show the incident and mitigation steps, AWS is usually more receptive to a larger ENI bump.

Sam: Good points. I'll open 4 cases (one per account-region pair for accelerator quotas, and ENI/ENIs for each account). Will request: p5->8, p4d->4, g5->20, ENI->2000. Asking for expedited review and include logs + ALB doc + expected launch date.

Ryan: Please cc billing and capacity-planning on the accelerator tickets so we can project spend and reserve if needed.

Sam: Will do. I'll post updates here when AWS responds. If any of these are delayed, fallback plan is to spin temporary Dedicated capacity in us-east-1 and replicate models there (will add ~25ms latency), but prefer regional capacity.

Maya: Thanks — please tag me on updates. If AWS asks for more data I can provide perf numbers and customer SLA doc.

Sam: Noted. Opening tickets now.
